''[[Appendix:Glossary#c.|c.]]'' '''1521''', [[:w:John Skelton|John Skelton]], Speke Parott:[[Category:English terms with quotations|ALAS]]
'''Helas''' I lamente the dull abuſyd brayne
The enfatuate fantaſies the wytles wylfulnes
Of on and hothyr at me that haue dyſdayne
[[Category:English terms with quotations|ALAS]]
#*
''[[Appendix:Glossary#c.|c.]]'' '''1599–1602''' (date written), [[:w:William Shakespeare|William Shakespeare]], “[[:w:Hamlet|The Tragedie of Hamlet, Prince of Denmarke]]”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] ([[:w:First Folio|First Folio]]), London: […] [[w:William Jaggard|Isaac Iaggard]], and [[w:Edward Blount|Ed[ward] Blount]], published 1623, [https://search.worldcat.org/title/606515358 →OCLC], [Act V, scene i], [https://archive.org/details/mrvvilliamshakes00shak/page/278/mode/1up page 278], column 1:[[Category:English terms with quotations|ALAS]]
'''Alas''' poore ''Yorick'', I knew him ''Horatio'', a fellow of infinite Ieſt; of moſt excellent fancy, he hath borne me on his backe a thouſand times: And how abhorred my Imagination is, my gorge riſes at it.
[[Category:English terms with quotations|ALAS]]
#*
'''1611''', [[w:Bible|The Holy Bible, […]]] ([[:w:King James Version|King James Version]]), London: […] [[w:Robert Barker (printer)|Robert Barker]], […], [https://search.worldcat.org/title/964384981 →OCLC], [[:w:Book of Revelation|Revelation]] [https://www.kingjamesbibleonline.org/1611_Revelation-Chapter-18/#10 18:10]:[[Category:English terms with quotations|ALAS]]
Standing afarre off for the feare of her torment, saying, '''Alas''', '''alas''', that great citie Babylon, that mighty citie: for in one houre is thy iudgement come.
[[Category:English terms with quotations|ALAS]]
#*
'''1920''', [[:w:Edward Carpenter|Edward Carpenter]], Pagan and Christian Creeds, New York: Harcourt, Brace and Co., published 1921, page 188:[[Category:English terms with quotations|ALAS]]
The thorough and shameless commercialism of Sex has '''alas'''! been reserved for what is called "Christian civilization," and with it (perhaps as a necessary consequence) Prostitution and Syphilis have grown into appalling evils, accompanied by a gigantic degradation of social standards, and upgrowth of petty Philistinism and ''niaiserie''.
[[Category:English terms with quotations|ALAS]]

 [[:w:alas (geography)|alas (geography)]] on Wikipedia
From [[w:Yakut language|Yakut]][[Category:English terms derived from Yakut|ALAS]] [[:алаас#Yakut|алаас]] (alaas). ====Pronunciation==== * [[Wiktionary:International Phonetic Alphabet|IPA]]([[Appendix:English pronunciation|key]]): /əˈlɑːs/, /əˈlæs/[[Category:English 2-syllable words|ALAS]][[Category:English 2-syllable words|ALAS]][[Category:English terms with IPA pronunciation|ALAS]] ====Noun==== alas (plural [[:alases#English|alases]] or [[:alasses#English|alasses]])[[Category:English lemmas|ALAS]][[Category:English nouns|ALAS]][[Category:English countable nouns|ALAS]][[Category:English entries with incorrect language header|ALAS]][[Category:Pages with entries|ALAS]][[Category:Pages with 27 entries|ALAS]] # A type of [[:geological#English|geological]] [[:depression#English|depression]] formed by the [[:subsidence#English|subsidence]] of [[:permafrost#English|permafrost]], sometimes (partially) filled by a [[lake]]. #: Alternative forms: [[:alass#English|alass]], [[:alaas#English|alaas]] #*
'''1973''', Arctic Bulletin, page 35:[[Category:English terms with quotations|ALAS]]
[…] '''alasses''' probably exist south of the Yukon Flats. Another bus tour went to the east, and '''alasses''' and pingos were examined on the terraces.
[[Category:English terms with quotations|ALAS]]
#*
'''2007''', Mary Chapman, The Geology of Mars: Evidence from Earth-Based Analogs, page 292:[[Category:English terms with quotations|ALAS]]
[…] '''alasses'''. They are formed when a large quantity of ground ice thaws (up to 80% by volume) in permafrost. '''Alasses''' are characteristics of the thermal degradation stages of permafrost. Their subsequent thaw induces a lowering of the [terrain].
[[Category:English terms with quotations|ALAS]]
#*
'''2018''', Colin K. Ballantyne, Periglacial Geomorphology, page 129:[[Category:English terms with quotations|ALAS]]
[…] permafrost (yedoma), the large volume loss that accompanies the melt of excess ice to produce an '''alas''' is irreversible, and secondary thermokarst lakes developed in ice-rich epigenetic permafrost on the '''alas''' floor are likely to be much smaller and shallower than the original thermokarst lake.
